agent_position: D20 as settled: a relay may be shared by several provisioning services, each bound to its own range; one relay per provisioning service rejected as a rule enforced only by documentation
owner_disposition: One relay per operator (per provisioning service), each with its own token, is the recommended deployment; a shared relay stays supported with its limits stated in the runbook and seller documentation: one token for every client lets root on any host log in from anywhere and exhaust the relay for every operator, rotating it touches every operator's hosts, and frps 0.61.1's admin API cannot end one client's sessions, so ending one operator's means restarting the relay under everyone; D21's open question concerns the shared arrangement only
summary: Owner made one relay per operator the recommended deployment, keeping shared relays supported with stated limits

summary: Owner added an emergency grant re-issue gap and a per-incident runbook choice in place of accepting refusals

agent_position: Gap recorded unowned at closeout, covering grant re-issue under a new key only; the keep-the-key option worded as an attacker holding the relay token signing within the operator's range

summary: Owner widened the emergency-rotation gap to the relay token and corrected who can sign under a kept key
